The strongest honest case for buying: the coin is alive, up 147% over 30 minutes, and in the last 15 minutes it drew 450 buyers against 240 sellers, 140 SOL bought versus 55 SOL sold, and net inflow of 85 SOL. It has not dipped from its 30-minute high (drawdown 0.03%), and pool depth is about 391 SOL, so a $20 ticket won't move the price much. Volume of roughly $23k in 15 minutes is real activity.

But the brief undercuts that case. The class is FACTORY, a bucket that has lost about 46% per trade. The curve is 100% bundle share with the top 3 buyers holding everything, and the first two minutes after graduation show 172 SOL from 54 buyers with a 0.04 sell-to-buy ratio and a launch bot present. That is coordinated supply accumulation, not organic demand. Recent buying looks like the bundle's exit liquidity being built, and a 0.03% drawdown from the high on a factory coin is more often a pause before distribution than a sign of support.

Verdict: I can't make a strong case to buy. Skip.

Bundle share is 1.0 and top3 share is 1.0, meaning the curve was filled entirely by coordinated wallets, and the top-5 buyer share of the first two minutes is 94%. A launch bot was present, and the completer share (2.87) suggests the supply was pre-positioned. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is only 0.04, but the last 15 minutes show 55 SOL sold against 140 bought, so exits have started. A ~3% round trip fee cost is also small against a coin that can reverse 30-50% in minutes. The name "SpaceX" borrows a famous brand, which tends to draw momentum buyers right before holders unload. Verdict: skip.
